title: Where the Stretch of Overdue Days Begins on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
A shop that has been told the guest wants the kit longer, or whose own records show the kit still being used after the date written on the agreement, does not count the overdue stretch from the date on the paper.

## The rule

Where the shop holds a request on the agreement to keep the kit to a later date, the stretch is counted from the day after the date the guest asked the kit to be kept to, through the date the kit reached the counter inclusive.

Where the shop holds no request on the agreement to keep the kit to a later date, and the rental account already carries a date the kit was out falling on or after the date written on the agreement, the stretch is counted from the day after the last date the account carries for the kit being out, through the date the kit reached the counter inclusive.

In any other case nothing under this heading changes how the stretch is counted.

## The two conditions in combination

| A request to keep the kit to a later date stands on the agreement | The account carries a date the kit was out on or after the date written on the agreement | The stretch runs from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | either way | the day after the date the guest asked the kit to be kept to |
| no | yes | the day after the last date the account carries for the kit being out |
| no | no | nothing under this heading changes it |

The request governs wherever it stands, whatever the dates out show. Only where no such request stands does the last date the kit was out come into it, and then only where that date falls on or after the date written on the agreement.

## Worked counts on hypothetical dates

Take an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement written to a due date of the 10th of January whose kit reached the counter on the 16th.

- A request stands on the agreement to keep the kit to the 13th: the stretch runs from the 14th through the 16th, which is 3 days.
- No request stands, and the last date the account carries for the kit being out is the 12th: the 12th falls after the 10th, so the stretch runs from the 13th through the 16th, which is 4 days.
- No request stands, and the last date the account carries for the kit being out is the 9th: the 9th falls before the 10th, so nothing under this heading changes the count.

In every case the stretch is never taken below zero, so a date the guest asked the kit to be kept to that falls on or after the date the kit reached the counter leaves no days in it.

## Point of judgement

**Which request is read.** The request read is the one standing on that agreement asking for the kit to be kept to a later date, and the date read from it is the date the guest asked the kit to be kept to.
